title: ESP IDE WebSocket message
description: Each WebSocket text message carries one JSON object. The IDE sets ESP_IDE_WS to the socket URL. A tool may set its own URL instead, such as esp-idf-monitor --ws. A diagnostic comes from any tool. Its type is "warning", "error", or "exception". An event comes from esp-idf-monitor. Its type is "event". The IDE replies with an event name such as "debug_finished". That reply can leave type out. Monitor checks the event name only. If the reply includes type, it must be "event".

diagnostic.description: Structured warning, error, or uncaught exception, sent by the tool. Hints, notes, and progress are not sent.

type.description: warning and error carry the console line as plain text, with Rich markup removed and without the WARNING: or ERROR: prefix. exception is an uncaught crash. SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt are not reported.

file.description: Python file that logged the message, or where the exception was raised. "<unknown>" if the file is not known. This is usually a file inside the tool, not the user's project.

line.description: Line number in file. The first line is 1. Use 0 if the line is not known.

message.description: Text to show the user. For exception, the exception text (which may be empty).

suggestion.description: Extra help text. It is not printed in the terminal. For a crash, this is the traceback, or null if there is none. For a warning or error, this is null unless the tool added a suggested fix.

event.description: A debug message between a tool and the IDE. Extra fields depend on the event name. esp-idf-monitor sends gdb_stub (port, prog), coredump (file, prog), and flash (port, target, full). It then waits for debug_finished or flash_finished. flash_finished may include success as true or false. Other event names are allowed.

type.description: Always present on events sent through esp-pylib. An IDE reply can leave it out. Legacy clients that do not use esp-pylib can also leave it out, so identify an event by its event field.

event.description: Name of the event. The other side waits for this name.
